prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Regional Dispatch Center (Juniper) intakes, triages, dispatches, coordinates under approved protocols; jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local policy. Juniper creates incident records, preserves reports/clarifications, tracks coverage, escalates gaps. Call Taker Mara (Larkspur) confirms/repeats location before medical details, distinguishes observed/reported facts, obtains pediatric age, available weight and caregiver observations, updates records before dispatch, produces Caller Location Correction Slip, confirms incident ID/receiving facility before destination requests, receives Bedside Arrival Receipt, verifies arrival time against dispatch timeline/crew communications. Computer Aided Dispatch Console presents incident, priority, maps, travel, availability, constraints, staging, surge; verify currency. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield) reviews uncertain/conflicting/deteriorating/severe cases; assigns/document priorities by immediacy, time sensitivity, deterioration risk; urgent threats get highest available priority/prompt dispatch. Sends Pediatric Acuity Note; advises demand repositioning; refers unusual cases to Regional Medical Director when time permits; approves/documents temporary triage overrides before application and reviews audit memo before duplicate closure. Regional Medical Director sets policy/advises clinical needs, elevated-demand priorities, specialized/protocol destinations; no dispatch authority. Data Quality Officer (Pebble) flags defects, audits completeness/compliance/rationales, sends Duplicate Incident Audit Memo, routes corrections, reviews incomplete arrival/handover fields and discrepancies through quality process without delaying care; cannot change priority. Ambulance Coordination Platform consolidates suitable units, timestamps status/movement, presents approved destination/instructions; selection considers priority, need, travel, capability/readiness, constraints, coverage; tracks accepted mutual-aid assignments separately. Juniper verifies battery readiness via swap voucher, congestion via queue snapshot. North Gate Status Board shows north access; South Gate Status Board shows southern routes/entries and produces South Access Lane Notice for material constraints. Dispatchers compare response times with remaining coverage. Shift Commander (Sundial) approves coverage-reducing/nonstandard exceptions, reviews staging/access/surge, sends Mutual Aid Release Form; after surge ensures assignments, destination constraints and staffing gaps handed over. Hospital Liaison Desk obtains capacity, coordinates destination consultation, records responses and informs dispatch of unresolved constraints; uses Pediatric Acuity Note. Kestrel confirms facility capacity/pediatric limits reach dispatch before destination finalization. Riverside Trauma Center advises liaison of trauma-intake suitability constraints. Emergency Department reports capacity/access/receiving changes, acknowledges destination changes and immediate restrictions, clarifies identity/transfer discrepancies with

Document units:
S202: If voice contact fails, dispatchers use the approved data channel when available and record the time of each attempted contact.
S203: Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays the latest confirmed unit status alongside the time and source of that confirmation.
S204: Ambulance Coordination Platform preserves queued status updates during brief connection interruptions and flags records that require reconciliation.
S205: Coverage monitoring compares successful radio checks with the planned check interval for each operating area.
S206: North Gate Status Board and South Gate Status Board provide separate views of access conditions that may affect radio reach or ambulance movement.
S207: Radio Coordinator uses the change card to adjust channel assignments and record the effective time of each change.
S208: Shift Commander receives the Coverage Gap Bulletin and decides whether staffing or deployment adjustments are needed.
S209: Data Quality Officer reviews Pebble for conflicting timestamps before interrupted communications are reconciled.
S210: Triage Supervisor identifies calls whose clinical priority requires immediate radio access and communicates that priority to dispatch staff.
S211: Call Taker Mara keeps the caller connected when feasible while dispatch staff attempt to reach the assigned crew through an approved alternate channel.
S212: Ambulance Unit 417 reports its last confirmed position and safe operating status as soon as contact is restored.
S213: Fleet Maintenance Cell reports radio equipment faults through the established maintenance escalation path.
S214: Hospital Liaison Desk uses available telephone channels to confirm whether receiving facilities can accept arrivals during a network disruption.
S215: Emergency Department staff receive concise arrival updates through the approved backup contact method when radio delivery is unavailable.
S216: Regional Medical Director may advise on clinical prioritization when communication limits materially affect response choices.
S217: Paramedic Crew members follow local safety procedures and do not enter an area where dispatch instructions cannot be confirmed if conditions are uncertain.
S218: Shift Commander retains operational authority until a named successor acknowledges the handover or a higher-level incident command arrangement takes effect.
S219: The outgoing shift records active incidents, communication failures, temporary channel assignments, and decisions awaiting review.
S220: The incoming shift verifies open assignments and confirms which communication paths remain available before accepting control.
S221: After service is restored, dispatch staff reconcile delayed status reports against their recorded timestamps and preserve any unresolved discrepancy for review.
S222: The Regional Dispatch Center maintains controlled procedures for reviewing operational records, approving system changes, and documenting corrective actions.
S223: The Data Quality Officer samples incident records for completeness, timestamp consistency, and alignment between dispatch decisions and recorded outcomes.
